questions.stem: Which organ produces both sperm and testosterone?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
The penis delivers semen; it makes neither cells nor hormone.
The duct transports sperm; production happens in the testis.
Glands add fluids; the testis makes the gametes and hormone.

questions.stem: Why do the testes hang in the scrotum outside the body?

options.text: To warm them above body temperature
options.explanation: The point is cooling, not warming.

options.text: To keep sperm slightly cooler than core body temperature
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: To keep them safe from urine
options.explanation: Urine never touches the testes.

options.text: To place them near the bladder
options.explanation: Closeness to the bladder is not the reason.

questions.stem: What prevents urine and semen mixing inside the male tract?

options.explanation: The taught gate is the urethral muscle ring.
Gland fluids join the semen; they do not gate urine.

options.text: A ring of muscle in the urethra
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The scrotum is outside the tract entirely.

questions.stem: What is added to sperm as they pass through the sperm duct?

options.explanation: Chromosomes are set; no additions happen in the duct.

options.text: Digestive enzymes for the egg coat
options.explanation: The taught addition is gland fluid forming semen.
Sperm use anaerobic-adjacent metabolism; no bubbles are added.
Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

questions.stem: During intercourse, which structure delivers semen into the vagina?

options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: The urethra of the bladder alone
options.explanation: The urethra runs through the penis; the delivery organ is the penis.
The scrotum supports testes; it never delivers semen.
The duct ends inside the tract, not in the vagina.

questions.stem: Name the hormone produced by the testes.
questions.modelAnswer: The testes produce testosterone as well as sperm.

questions.stem: State the two liquids the urethra can carry.
questions.modelAnswer: The urethra can carry urine or semen.

questions.stem: Explain why the position of the scrotum outside the body is an adaptation for sperm production.
questions.modelAnswer: Making sperm needs a temperature a little below core body heat, and the scrotum supplies that by holding the testes outside.

questions.stem: A patient's swollen tissue raises testicular temperature. Predict the effect on sperm production and justify it.
questions.modelAnswer: Sperm production should fall, since the testes rely on being slightly cooler than core body heat, and the swelling erases that cooling.

questions.stem: Where are the ova stored and matured before release?

options.explanation: The cervix is the muscular gate, not a nursery.

options.text: In the ovaries, maturing as hormones are released
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Oviducts transport ova; they do not mature them.
The lining hosts implantation, not egg maturation.

questions.stem: What pushes the released ovum along the oviduct?

options.explanation: The vagina is below the tract's transport section.
The cervix holds the fetus; it does not ferry ova.

options.text: The ciliated cells lining the oviduct
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Ova have no tails; sperm do.

questions.stem: Which structure is described as a muscular sac with a soft lining where an embryo implants?

options.explanation: The oviduct is a narrow tube for transport and fertilisation.
The ovary makes and releases ova.
The vagina receives sperm; implantation does not happen there.
Correct — this matches the account taught above.

questions.stem: What role does the cervix play during pregnancy?

options.text: Its ring of muscle keeps the developing fetus in place
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Ova release is ovarian.
Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct.

options.text: It lines the uterus for implantation
options.explanation: The soft uterine lining does that, not the cervix.

questions.stem: Sperm deposited during intercourse reach the egg by travelling through which sequence?

options.explanation: That reverses the actual path.

options.text: Vagina, then cervix, then uterus, then oviduct
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
The cervix and uterus lie between.
Deposition is in the vagina; entry order starts there.

questions.stem: Name the tube that connects the ovary to the uterus.
questions.modelAnswer: The oviduct connects the ovary to the uterus and is lined with ciliated cells.

questions.stem: State where fertilisation occurs in the female reproductive system.
Explain why the oviduct's ciliated lining is an adaptation for its function.
questions.modelAnswer: The cilia push the released ovum along the tube toward the uterus, ensuring the egg travels to where fertilisation and implantation can follow.

questions.stem: An infection damages the cilia of the oviducts. Predict two consequences and explain them.
questions.modelAnswer: The ovum may fail to travel toward the uterus, lowering the chance of fertilisation in the oviduct, since the cilia are what push the released ovum along.
